title: Handoff scribbles — night SRE shift (Erin)
content:
Quick handoff notes from the night shift. Mostly a scratchpad — leave comments in Slack or update the runbook directly.

Shift summary:
- Window: 2026-03-15 22:00 -> 2026-03-16 06:00 (PST).
- Pager volume: higher than baseline for DB read/replica lag alerts and api-generator latency spikes between 23:10-00:05.
- Primary incidents: INC-5173 (API generation latency spikes, cascading autoscaler thrash).
- No data exfil or PII exposure. All customer-facing degradations were transient; some timed-out user requests (5xx) for ~20m.

INC-5173 — timeline & actions (short):
- 23:05: first page: multiple pod restarts observed in gen-service (k8s restarts 5xx).
- 23:10: alerted on elevated p50/p95 token latency for hosted API route /v1/generate.
- 23:12: manually scaled gen-service from HPA recommended 6 -> 10 replicas (kubectl scale deploy/gen-service --replicas=10).
- 23:18: observed improvement in tail latency but repeat restarts persisted for 2 pods.
- 23:25: rolled back micro-deploy (git tag: release/2026-03-15-22:40) which contained a faulty hot-path change to attention cache logic. Rollback completed 23:29.
- 23:35: CORE: tail latency returned to baseline; no new restarts. Post-incident: left pods at 8 replicas pending autoscaler tune.

Hypothesis / root cause (working):
- Recent micro-release introduced narrower KV-cache lifecycle that allowed cache churn under high-concurrency patterns -> memory bump + OOM restarts for gen-service on certain sequence-length distributions.
- HPA thresholds combined with aggressive scale-down caused thrash during the spike.
- Secondary: we saw a small uptick in prefix-cache-miss rate on redis proxy (see graphs) which amplified token generation latencies.

Immediate mitigations taken (and why):
- rollback release/2026-03-15-22:40 -> safe fast path. (stops buggy code path).
- manual scale up to dampen autoscaler oscillation while we assess.
- temporarily increased alert thresholds for gen-service cpu OOMs to avoid noisy pages (not ideal long-term).

Follow-ups & TODOs (assign/notes):
- [ ] SRE-204: Add test case to staging for high-concurrency + mixed sequence-length workload to reproduce cache churn (owner: Samir Rao) — target: 2026-03-22.
- [ ] Update gen-service runbook: add rollback checklist, include quick kubectl diff commands, and add sample query to check prefix-cache-hit-rate (owner: Erin) — due 2026-03-18.
- [ ] Tune HPA scaleDown stabilizationPeriod and targetUtilization to reduce oscillation for gen-service (owner: infra-team; ticket: INFRA-799) — discuss Monday ops sync.
- [ ] Add a synthetic smoke test that runs 50 parallel generate requests with varied seq lengths every 15m in canary region (owner: Lena Chen) — PR w/ sched job pending.
- [ ] Investigate redis proxy metrics around 22:50-23:30 (owner: observability) — link graphs to SRE-204.

Runbook quick edits (notes to self):
- Insert command snippets: 
  - kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/gen-service --to-revision=2026-03-14-12
  - kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide --selector=app=gen-service | grep CrashLoop
  - redis-cli -h redis-proxy-01 info keyspace | grep prefix_cache
- Add 'when to roll back vs patch' section — decision tree: severity >15% error rate for >10m -> rollback; else try patch.

Paging behavior observations:
- Alerts that page during this incident:
  - A) api.v1.generate.p95_latency > 3000ms for >3m
  - B) k8s.pod.crashloop_count >=2 within 5m
  - C) redis.proxy.prefix_cache_miss > 0.2 sustained for 5m
- A and B together should escalate to primary oncall + infra pager. C alone is SRE list (slack only).
- Note: we had an alert combo that matched A+B then flapped; need to re-evaluate escalation policy to avoid duplicate pages.

Useful commands & quick queries used tonight (copyable):
- kubectl -n prod get hpa gen-service -o yaml | yq '.spec'
- kubectl -n prod get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 60
- prometheus query (for tail latency): sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",le=+Inf}[5m])) by (le)
- grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/gen-service?from=1640995200000&to=1672531199000 (replace time params)

Notes for next oncall (what I'd do first):
- Check gen-service pods for CrashLoopBackOff. If yes, check /var/log/gen-service/current.log for OOM traces.
- If OOM -> rollback and scale up to 8 while we patch.
- If no crashloops but high latency -> confirm redis prefix cache miss rates then try manual scale up before touching code.
- Remember to leave short note in #oncall-night when you start and when you hand off.

Open tickets created tonight:
- INC-5173 (incident doc) — initial writeup, timeline, graph snapshots attached.
- SRE-204 (postmortem + remediation tasks) — links to PRs for runbook and tests.

Loose thoughts / rough ideas (brain dump):
- Could we add an adaptive stabilization period to HPA specifically for gen-service type workloads that are bursty? (algorithm idea: increase scaleDown delay proportional to recent restart count).
- Consider prefix-cache warmers during high-traffic windows to reduce cold-miss amplification.
- Is there room for more graceful degradation: short-circuit non-critical features during tail-latency spikes (e.g., lower top-k sampling).

Final: leaving system in steady state, autoscaler left at replicas=8 for 2 hrs then reverted to HPA. Logged rollback and actions in INC-5173. Ping me if you need context.

Erin

(rough — will tidy into SRE-204 PM notes tomorrow)
